ladder.teaches: a set to remember what you have seen
ladder.why: The smallest possible hashing problem: one pass, one set, 'have I seen this before?' answered in O(1).

ladder.teaches: a map from value to index (look up the complement)
ladder.why: Turns 'find a pair' into 'look up the complement': store value -> index for what is behind you and ask for target - x.
Order disappears once you count: two strings match when their letter counts match.

ladder.teaches: a canonical key to group things (sorted string, count signature)
ladder.why: A count signature is the same for every anagram, so it can be a dictionary key that groups them.

ladder.teaches: buckets indexed by frequency or value
ladder.why: Frequencies are bounded by n, so an array of buckets indexed by count replaces a full sort.

ladder.teaches: a set to remember what you have seen
ladder.why: A set gives O(1) membership; only starting runs at values with no predecessor keeps the whole scan O(n).

ladder.teaches: the array index as the hash (in-place marking)
ladder.why: When values lie in 1..n the array can be its own set: the sign of nums[v] records 'seen v'.

ladder.teaches: a map from value to index (look up the complement)
ladder.why: Complement lookup in an Amazon OA story, with duplicates and k = 0 to handle by thinking in distinct values.
Only how many copies of a value exist matters, so a count map plus a running sum answers each update in O(1).
Recognise that fixing the shared digit turns the question into ten simple counts.

ladder.teaches: a map from value to index (look up the complement)
ladder.why: Instead of comparing all pairs, generate each number's few neighbours and look them up in a frequency map.

ladder.teaches: a canonical key to group things (sorted string, count signature)
ladder.why: A prefix's count vector divided by its gcd is a canonical key that finds the earlier prefixes where cuts can go.
A counting insight: distinct reversals correspond to pairs of different letters, computed from 26 frequencies.

ladder.teaches: the array index as the hash (in-place marking)
ladder.why: Index-as-hash under an O(1)-space rule: cyclic swaps put each v at index v-1, then the first gap is the answer.

notes: Every technique covered. vanguard-two-sum moved here from the sorting pool (canonical Two Sum with a unique pair, so the one-pass map is exactly right; amazon-two-sum's lexicographic tie rule defeats the one-pass map). akuna-items-sort moved to sorting. Several core classics (Contains Duplicate, Valid Anagram, Top K Frequent, Longest Consecutive, Find the Duplicate, First Missing Positive) were in no pool and were taken in. amazon-most-common-product-pair skipped: the statement does not say what to return when no pair exists. The bank has no clean 'find all disappeared numbers' easy for index marking, so spacex-duplicate-number carries it.
